scope: T2b primary jitter and depth/motion consistency; diagnostic only, no temporal resolve
hardware: Linux x86-64; AMD Radeon 880M Graphics (RADV STRIX1); Vulkan; radv; Mesa 26.2.5-arch1.1

settings.requires: resolved motion-vector diagnostics and HDR; unmet prerequisites fall back to zero jitter with a note
settings.primary_consumers: regular/conforming terrain and rigid mesh raster only
settings.sequence: existing Halton(2,3), each axis at most 0.5 output pixel; increment only on submitted real frame; reset/resize clears previous camera and restarts the sequence
settings.secondary_consumers: classifier, conforming policy, shadows, RT geometry, clear sky, translucent overlays and HUD retain unjittered views
settings.visible_behavior: jitter is deliberately visible without a resolve; enabling prints a warning, not a TAA/antialiasing claim

motion_contract.reconstruction: current raster UV/depth with its matching jittered inverse
motion_contract.future_history_sampling: add previous jitter to the reprojected unjittered source UV; previous-jitter history retention and resolve remain T4 work
motion_contract.dynamic_masks: ocean and all rigid meshes remain invalid; jitter is not object motion
motion_contract.stationary_camera: changing sampling jitter must not produce camera velocity

regressions.cpu: known point reconstruction with matching jittered inverse; incorrect unjittered-inverse convention rejected; finite/range/layout validation; settings roundtrip and prerequisites
regressions.gpu_scene: existing actual regular/conforming scene oracle extended to moving and stationary cameras, seven frames, two water material cases, Low/High mesh shaders, reset/resize and projection/exposure changes; disabled-jitter RGB identity and enabled-jitter primary visibility change
regressions.sky: exact clear-sky framebuffer identity over eight primary jitter samples, plus rejection when jitter was not resolved
regressions.topology: eight jittered blocks leave the conforming policy and generation exactly unchanged; test does not assume arbitrary warmup establishes quiescence
regressions.initial_test_failure: target/temporal-t2b-motion.log retains a failed assertion that 24 near-surface CBT warmup iterations must settle. That assumption was invalid. Replaced with exact policy/generation invariance in the existing topology hardware oracle; no quiescence or renderer speedup claim.

verification.status: all local gates and release captures passed; all 18 pinned source inputs unchanged
verification.input_manifest: target/temporal-t2b-inputs.json pins 18 modified Rust/WGSL/TOML source/config/test inputs
verification.bevy_ignored: required command ran and selected zero tests; this crate has no ignored tests in this checkout, not eight hardware passes

release_captures.baseline: same release binary with jitter off and motion diagnostics on, not an unmodified parent executable
release_captures.extra_runs: 16-frame --sweep headless capture with jitter on and sim-step 0; eight real window frames with HUD/no HUD, both muted and reporting jitter=true; all exited 0
release_captures.limits: Four serial blocks only; streaming, scheduling and thermal noise not eliminated. No stable whole-frame regression or speedup claim. No TAA quality or subjective preference result.

deliberately_omitted: No TAA/TAAU, colour history, previous jitter for history, disocclusion or complete camera/source/light epochs.
No SDK/FG or simulation/autopilot/alarm advancement from presentation.
No aesthetic improvement or independent blind preference votes for an intentionally unresolved diagnostic; numeric correctness is separate from preference.
No resolved-depth/reactive-mask solution for unjittered translucent overlays clipping against sampled depth, universal precision envelope or peak driver/VRAM budget.
